sentences.text: This large therizinosaurid dinosaur reached a length of nearly 5 meters and a mass between 600 and 907 kilograms.
Its skeleton featured stocky posterior neck vertebrae with opisthocoel centra, a condition where the rear of the bone is concave.
The animal possessed a strong, pot-bellied build supported by stout hindlimbs and a foot that functioned with four toes.
A well-preserved axis vertebra measured 13.5 centimeters in length and displayed platycoelus centra, which are slightly concave at both ends.
The seventh and eighth cervical vertebrae were the longest in the neck, with centra measuring 18 centimeters.
The pelvis was opisthopubic, meaning the pubis and ischium bones were fused and directed backward.
The ilium was stocky and featured an extremely well-developed, elongated preacetabular process but lacked a postacetabular process.
This bulky high-browser shared its environment with various oviraptorosaur species.
The ecosystem included the tyrannosaurid Qianzhousaurus, the sauropod Gannansaurus, and sparse remains of the hadrosaurid Microhadrosaurus.
Contemporary fauna also comprised nanhsiungchelyid turtles, squamates like Chianghsia and Tianyusaurus, and the crocodilian Jiangxisuchus.
The genus was formally described by Dong Zhiming in 1979.
The type species, Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, was discovered in 1974 and officially named in 1979.
Fossil remains were found during an expedition at the Nanxiong Basin in Guangdong Province.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as IVPP V4731, includes twelve cervical, ten dorsal, six sacral, and the first caudal vertebrae along with a nearly complete pelvis.
The initial collection was made by a team from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
Early researchers initially mistook this creature for a small, strange sauropod with a shorter but thicker neck than typical members of that group.
Estimates for the species Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus suggest a length of 4.4 to 5 meters and a weight ranging from 454 to 907 kilograms.
In contrast, Paul estimated the doubtful second species, Nanshiungosaurus bohlini, to be 6 meters long and weigh 1.3 tonnes, noting fused cervical ribs as a distinguishing feature.
Nanshiungosaurus is classified as a therizinosaurid dinosaur that lived in South China.
Early studies of therizinosaurs were difficult due to sparse remains, leading some scientists to interpret them as prosauropod dinosaurs.
In 1979, Dong assigned the genus to Titanosaurinae based on the assumption that it was a sauropod.
However, a 2010 analysis by Zanno concluded that the family Nanshiungosauridae was invalid and merely a synonym of Therizinosauridae.
A phylogenetic analysis by Hartman et al. in 2019 recovered Nanshiungosaurus as a therizinosaurid in a more derived position than Erliansaurus or Neimongosaurus.
The parent group of this genus is Therizinosauridae.
Fossils were found in the Nanxiong Formation, dated to about 66.7 ± 0.3 million years ago in the latest Maastrichtian stage.
This dinosaur was one of the last therizinosaurids to exist.
The time range for Nanshiungosaurus spans from the Albian to the Maastrichtian, between 113.2 and 66 million years ago.
A second species, "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini, was described in 1997 based on remains found in 1992, but its validity is unsupported.
It is debated whether "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini belongs to the genus, as the original describers provided no evidence or argumentation to support the assignment.
There is a scientific consensus that the specimen "Nanshiungosaurus" bohlini is no longer considered related to the main genus Nanshiungosaurus.
Further debate exists regarding the assignment due to significant age differences from the type species and issues with authentic characteristics.
Dong and Yu provided no evidence or argumentation to support the assignment of the species to Nanshiungosaurus.
Due to a lack of shared unique traits and the large age difference with Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, the supposed second species is generally considered unrelated and could justify its own genus.
